title: app-shell: the exported DefaultLoginPage and DefaultRegisterPage still offer generic sign-up under the invite_only audience posture (the objectui#11691 defect, on the published default pages)
body:
Filing gate ①: a product defect with a named location and a named producer.

Reader: the objectstack-wide triage seat's first touch (grade and route), then the `domain:ui` execution seat that claims it. The fix lands in `@object-ui/app-shell`'s exported default auth pages.

Dedupe: `mcp__github__search_issues` on objectstack-ai/objectui, closed included: "DefaultLoginPage DefaultRegisterPage sign up link invite_only audience posture app-shell default auth pages" gives 9 hits. None of them is this defect:
- objectui#11691 is the console's own pages (this card's sibling, in flight);
- objectui#11634, #11058, #11030, #10998, #4233, #2625 and #2416 are closed, and each covers a different defect;
- objectui#11649 is a different surface.
The positive control for the query: #11058 and #11030 are earlier cards on these same two exported pages.

## What happens

`/api/v1/auth/config` states the sign-up rule in two keys: `emailPassword.disableSignUp` and `features.audiencePosture`. Under the default `invite_only` posture the server keeps `disableSignUp: false` on purpose, so that a pending invitee can still register. It refuses an uninvited sign-up with `403 SELF_REGISTRATION_CLOSED`. objectui#11691 (PR objectui#11703) makes the console's own `/login` and `/register` read both keys.

`@object-ui/app-shell` also publishes `DefaultLoginPage` and `DefaultRegisterPage`, and these still read `disableSignUp` alone.

- **Reach, named producer:** `examples/console-starter/src/App.tsx` routes `DefaultLoginPage` at `/login` and `DefaultRegisterPage` at `/register`.
- **Measured** by the objectui#11691 dev with a throwaway render probe, not committed (report on objectui#11691):
  - With `audiencePosture: 'invite_only'` and `disableSignUp: false`, `DefaultLoginPage` renders the "Sign up" link and `DefaultRegisterPage` renders the full form, which the server then refuses.
  - The control leg, `disableSignUp: true`, hides the link.

## Done when

- The exported default pages offer generic sign-up only where the server would accept it, by the same rule the console pages use after objectui#11691 lands. One decision serves both apps, with no second copy of the predicate.
- The pins cover `invite_only` with no "Sign up", an invitation redirect still reaching registration, `open` unchanged, and `disableSignUp: true` hiding everything.

Related: objectui#11691 (its decision, `apps/console/src/pages/auth/signUpOffer.ts` in PR objectui#11703, could be lifted into a package both apps import). Not dispatchable before objectui#11691's PR lands, because that PR settles the rule this card follows.
